title: Business Spec
description: A business spec (BIZ): one coherent product capability or behavior, with its individual rules captured as acceptance criteria. Extracted from the PRD.

title.description: One-line business description. Imperative, directive, no filler

description.description: Multi-paragraph narrative. What problem this solves, who is affected, what user-visible behaviour is expected. Technical implementation lives in plan.md, not here.

acceptance_criteria.description: Verifiable acceptance criteria. Each begins with an implementation checkbox — `[ ]` not implemented, `[x]` implemented — then a commitment level. Order by commitment level: MUST, then MUST NOT, then SHOULD, then SHOULD NOT, then MAY.

items.description: A single verifiable acceptance criterion. Starts with an implementation checkbox (`[ ]` or `[x]`) followed by a commitment level. `spex coverage` reads the checkbox to report how many of an active spec's criteria are implemented.

scope.description: Workspace repository names targeted for implementing this spec. Each must match a repository_name in spex.yaml.

blocked_by.description: Spec IDs (BIZ or TECH) that must be in place before this spec can be implemented. List only genuine blockers that are not yet satisfied; remove one once it ships or is established. Absent or empty means nothing blocks this spec. Do not list a shared foundation that every capability rides on (e.g. the API surface) — only the specs whose absence prevents this one from being built.

items.description: A BIZ or TECH spec ID that blocks this spec: this spec cannot be implemented until that spec is in place.

status.description: Lifecycle status. Omitting is equivalent to 'planned'.

coverage_ignore.description: Coverage layers to skip for this spec. A listed layer is treated as ok even when its annotation is missing, so it never counts as a gap. By default coverage requires all three layers.

examples.title: Allow customers to place an order from their cart
examples.description:
Customers who have added items to their cart need a way to complete a purchase. When a customer confirms checkout, the system creates an order from the current cart contents, captures payment, and empties the cart.

This affects all authenticated shoppers. After a successful order, the customer should see an order confirmation with a unique order number.
acceptance_criteria: [x] MUST create an order only when the cart contains at least one item
[x] MUST capture payment before the order is marked as confirmed
[ ] MUST empty the customer's cart after the order is successfully placed
[ ] SHOULD display an order confirmation with a unique order number
